info.title: pika/pika-2.5-text-to-video
info.description: The request body Comfy Router accepts for the model "pika/pika-2.5-text-to-video", and the response body it returns. The INPUT schema is the same schema the server validates a call against before it reaches the provider, so what is published and what is enforced cannot differ. `x-comfy-router-input-modalities` records the media kinds the model is documented to accept; the request schema is shared across sibling models and may admit media kinds this model ignores. The OUTPUT schema describes the provider's native result document exactly as Router returns it: Router does not validate, narrow or re-envelope the response, so the output schema is descriptive rather than enforced, and Comfy owns no output shape of its own.

schema.description: Request body for Pika 2.5 text-to-video: generate a five-second video from a text prompt. Comfy Router forwards this body to Pika's `pika/pika-2.5/text-to-video` endpoint unchanged and polls the job on the caller's behalf, so the response is the finished job document. A body outside the bounds declared here is refused with `422 invalid_input` before any provider is dialled.

example.prompt: A paper boat drifting down a rain-soaked city street at dusk

duration_s.description: Video length in seconds. Text-to-video produces five-second clips only.

negative_prompt.description: Text describing what to avoid in the video.

prompt.description: Text prompt describing the video to generate.

seed.description: Seed for reproducible generation. Omit it (or send null) for a random seed.

200.description: OK - the model's native JSON output, returned unchanged; the schema describes the provider's terminal result document as Router returns it.

schema.description: Pika's job document, the response for every Pika model Comfy Router serves. All of them are SUBMIT-AND-POLL: Router polls Pika's job status route on the caller's behalf, so the body a caller receives is the TERMINAL document rather than the queued handle the submit answers with. A caller therefore reads `status: "completed"` with the result under `output` — `output.images[].url` for an image model, `output.video.url` for a video model, or `output.videos[].url` when Pika delivers the video job as a list (`media_type: videos`), which Router treats as the same success. A job Pika fails, or one that completes without its media, does NOT come back as this document: Router answers it with its own error response instead. `queued`, `running` and `failed` are states of Pika's job that Router does not return in this body. Pika's own `billing` record is removed before the document reaches the caller; the credits a call consumed are reported on the response's `X-Comfy-Credits-Used` header.

model_id.description: The Pika catalog entry the job ran.

runtime_s.description: Seconds the generation took, from dispatch to terminal. Best-effort; may be null.

status.description: Lifecycle state. A body Router returns always reads `completed`; a `failed` job is answered with Router's error response instead.

usage.description: Provider-reported units for the job. Keys are sparse; only the units the job reports are present.

PikaRouterJobError.description: Pika's structured failure record, set on a `failed` job. Router answers a failed job with its own error response, so a body Router returns does not carry it; it is declared because it is part of Pika's job document.

PikaRouterJobOutput.description: The finished job's media, set when `status` is `completed`. `media_type` says which field carries it: `image` fills `images`, `video` fills `video`, and `videos` fills `videos`.

images.description: Generated images, for an image model.

seed.description: The seed the video job actually used, when reported.

videos.description: Generated videos, for a multi-video delivery.

url.description: Download URL of the generated file.
